issues.legal_issue: A landlord may pursue eviction under a replacement rent-control enactment for subletting that occurred while the repealed enactment was in force.
material_facts: The tenant’s alleged subletting occurred before the 1959 rent-control enactment was repealed.
The landlord instituted the eviction proceeding after the 1965 enactment came into force.
The former enactment permitted an eviction application on the ground of unauthorized subletting, and the replacement enactment contained an analogous provision.
issues.conclusion: The saving provision allowed the landlord to pursue eviction under the corresponding provision of the replacement enactment for subletting that occurred under the former enactment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34(1) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, including its proviso, preserved proceedings that could have been brought under the repealed Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1959, for institution under corresponding provisions of the new Act. Section 4 of the Kerala Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125, also applied because no contrary intention appeared. The former Act’s section 11(4) was a corresponding provision to the new Act’s section 11(4): corresponding means similar or analogous, not identical. The new Act’s section 11(1) did not displace that saving.

rule.if: post_repeal_eviction_proceeding and pre_repeal_subletting and old_law_subletting_ground and analogous_new_law_ground

predicates.post_repeal_eviction_proceeding: A landlord instituted an eviction proceeding after a former rent-control enactment had been replaced.
predicates.pre_repeal_subletting: The tenant sublet the premises before the former enactment was replaced.
predicates.old_law_subletting_ground: The former enactment permitted eviction proceedings on the ground of unauthorized subletting.
predicates.analogous_new_law_ground: The replacement enactment contained a provision analogous to the former enactment’s subletting ground.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is instituted after replacement of a rent-control enactment, prior subletting remains a ground for eviction if the former enactment allowed eviction for it and the replacement enactment has an analogous ground.

issues.legal_issue: A rent-control revisional court whose authority extends to legality, regularity, and propriety may examine whether a lower court’s factual finding is proper, rather than being confined to jurisdictional errors.
material_facts: The parties sought revision before the District Court under the rent-control enactment after the Subordinate Judge ruled on the eviction application.
The District Judge reconsidered the evidence concerning subletting and reversed the Subordinate Judge’s finding.
The High Court later confirmed the District Judge’s order.
issues.conclusion: The revisional authority under section 20 was not limited to jurisdictional questions and empowered the District Court to consider whether the finding on the evidence was proper. Because the High Court had confirmed the order, the Supreme Court did not examine whether the District Court had properly exercised that revisional power in this case.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20(1) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, empowered the District Court to examine records to satisfy itself as to the legality, regularity, or propriety of an order or proceeding and to pass an appropriate order. Its wording was wider than section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and did not confine revision to jurisdictional questions.

predicates.rent_control_revision: A party brought a revision from an order or proceeding under a rent-control enactment.
predicates.revisional_power_includes_propriety: The revisional authority was empowered to examine the propriety of the challenged order or proceeding and make an appropriate order.

issues.definition: When a rent-control revision is governed by authority to examine propriety, the revisional court may review whether a factual finding is proper.

issues.legal_issue: Evidence of a third party’s exclusive occupation of part of leased premises, considered with other circumstances, can support a finding of subletting despite rent being paid daily.
material_facts: The premises had been let as a lodging house.
A lawyer had occupied one room for years and was found to have exclusive possession of it.
The lawyer displayed a name board outside the room and had installed a telephone there.
The lawyer paid rent on a daily basis.
The District Court and High Court accepted the evidence as establishing subletting.
issues.conclusion: There was sufficient evidence to find subletting; daily rent did not make the arrangement a licence on these facts. The Supreme Court did not interfere with the concurrent findings of the District Court and High Court.
issues.legal_principle: In applying the subletting ground in section 11(4) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, the Court treated evidence of exclusive possession, together with the circumstances of occupation, as sufficient to support a finding of subletting rather than a licence. Daily payment of rent did not compel the conclusion that the arrangement was a licence. No earlier cases were relied on for this issue.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_concurrent_subletting_finding and third_party_exclusive_occupation and occupation_was_longstanding and third_party_displayed_name_board and third_party_installed_telephone and rent_was_paid_daily

predicates.appeal_challenges_concurrent_subletting_: An appeal challenges concurrent lower-court findings that a tenant sublet leased premises.
predicates.third_party_exclusive_occupation: A third party occupied part of the leased premises with exclusive possession.
predicates.occupation_was_longstanding: The third party had occupied that part of the premises for a substantial period.
predicates.third_party_displayed_name_board: The third party displayed a name board outside the occupied space.
predicates.third_party_installed_telephone: The third party installed a telephone in the occupied space.
predicates.rent_was_paid_daily: The third party paid rent on a daily basis.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges concurrent findings of subletting and the third party’s exclusive, longstanding occupation is accompanied by the stated indicators, the finding is upheld even if rent was paid daily.
